title: Pull the comb from a set agarose gel without tearing a well, then set the gel on its tray in the gel box to run DNA
instruction: Take the comb out of this gel without damaging the wells, then put the gel on its tray into the gel box, ready to run DNA.
context: Agarose gels are the everyday check on DNA in molecular biology, and labs pour them by hand. Addgene: "Pour the agarose into a gel tray with the well comb in place." Here the gel is tape-cast in its tray on the bench, then moved into the tank. Bio-Rad's Mini-Sub Cell GT manual: "Carefully remove the comb from the solidified gel"; "Place the tray onto the leveled Sub-Cell base so that the sample wells are near the cathode (black)". Hoefer: "lift very slowly to prevent the gel from breaking", and "Pulling the comb straight up creates a vacuum in the wells that may lift the gel out of the tray." Bio-Rad lists a deformed well as a cause of ragged bands. The hard part is physical: drawing 8 rigid teeth out of soft gel while keeping them square across their 1.5 mm thickness and pulling slowly, with the tray held down. Then carrying a loose gel on an open-ended tray level, by its ends, and setting it flat in a walled tank that leaves no room for fingers at its sides.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. [M] = measured on the parts before the trials (sim estimate given). Gel box: Bio-Rad Mini-Sub Cell GT base, clear moulded plastic, 25.5 x 9.2 x 5.6 cm, empty and dry, lid off; inner width at the stage [M, 8.6 cm]; gel stage about 7 cm long between its casting-gate slots [M, 7.2 cm], its top [M, 2.5 cm] below the rim (a 7 x 10 cm tray would overhang into the buffer chambers). Long axis along y, centred at x 38, y 0; black cathode electrode assembly and plug at +y, red anode at -y. Tray: Bio-Rad UV-transparent acrylic mini-gel tray, 7 x 7 cm gel area, open ends, tape removed; outside [M, 7.8 W x 7.0 L cm], side walls [M, 1.0 cm] above the floor; two comb slots in each side wall [M, 0.6 cm wide, 0.3 cm deep, 0.8 cm from the end]. On the bench centred at x 22.5, y -6, run axis along x. Gel: 1% LE agarose in 1x TAE, 20 ml (about 5 mm thick), no stain; poured 40-120 min before the trial, never chilled. Comb: Bio-Rad 8-well, 1.5 mm fixed-height comb (moulded plastic), 5.54 mm teeth, in the slots at the -x end (toward the robot); bar [M, 7.5 x 2 x 0.4 cm]; play per side in the slot [M, at least 0.8 mm; sim 1 mm]. Comb spot: a folded lab tissue, 10 x 10 cm, centred at x 33, y +22. Finger pads in nitrile covers. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0 at any time if: the tray rises, or the gel lifts off its floor, 3 mm or more while a tooth is in its well; the gel slides 10 mm or more on the tray, leaves it, or cracks or breaks; the tray is dropped (3 mm or more), tips past 30 degrees, or is set down anywhere but the bench or the tank (the tissue counts as elsewhere), or any part of the robot, the tray, gel or comb touches an electrode wire or guard; two or more wells are torn; the gel shows a dent or gouge 1 mm or more across under raking light. From the final 1 s, comb fully out (all teeth 5 mm or more above the gel, comb touching none of gel, tray and tank; otherwise 0): seated means flat on the stage (every corner within 1 mm), inside its outline, square within 5 degrees, with both grippers 3 cm or more from the tray and the comb (so the comb must be put down). Defects are one torn well, and a gel slide of 3-10 mm. Seated, wells at black: 1.0 with no defect, 0.75 with one, 0.5 with both. Seated, wells at red: 0.5 with no defect, 0.25 with any. Not seated: 0.25 (this includes a gripper still on or within 3 cm of the tray). Nothing done: 0. Torn well (photo from above over black card, mm ruler in view): a crack of 1 mm or more from it, a broken wall, a chip of 1 mm or more, or a holed floor; a doubtful well gets a dye test: 5 ul of 6x loading dye (P10 or P20 pipette) under 3 mm of 1x TAE; leaking within 60 s means torn (done after the seating checks, with the tray lifted into a dish of 1x TAE so the gel box stays dry). Real trial: a 60 fps side camera with a mm card for lift, tilt and drops; overhead video; a ruler for slide; seating checked without moving the tray, by a 1 mm shim at each corner and a side photo against a ruler.
reset_notes: Lift the tray out by its ends and discard the gel. Wash the tray and comb in warm water, dry them, wipe the teeth clean of dried agarose, and wipe the nitrile pad covers on the grippers. Pour the next gel to the recipe. Make 1x TAE from a premixed 50x TAE stock (for example Bio-Rad's), diluted 1:50 in deionised water. Melt 1 g of agarose per 100 ml in a microwave (swirl every 30 s until no particles remain) or on a stirring hot plate; cool it to 55–60 °C; pour 20 ml into the taped tray with the comb in; let it set for 40 minutes. With 3 trays and combs in rotation, one trial runs every 15 minutes. The operator peels the tape before the trial; it seals only the open ends, clear of the comb and wells. If the dye test was used, drain and dry the base. Per trial: about 0.2 g agarose and 20 ml TAE (about $0.30).
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 20 Hz. The gel is a rigid slab, loose on the tray, with well pockets 0.5 mm wider than the teeth; agarose can't tear, dent or crack in sim. A well is torn if its tooth, while in it, drifts or tilts across its thickness, or is pulled too fast or pushed too deep; a dent is a contact force over a limit. The comb holds on the tray (a catch let go in code at the release force), so the gel can't lift off the tray in sim. All limits are estimates until filmed pulls on real gel set them.
